w: The definitive Mission burrito since 1973 — no rice, seared meat, lines down the block. The carne asada super burrito is the one to get.

dish: al pastor / carne asada super burrito
w: Infatuation names it SF's best burrito outright — a nearly two-pound super burrito with charred carne asada and ideal ratios of guac, cheese, crema. Open since 1983.

dish: carnitas burrito mojado (wet burrito, red chili sauce)
w: Classic Mission taqueria; the carnitas burrito mojado doused in red chili with red and green salsa is big enough to split.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-francisco/guides/best-burrito-san-francisco — 'get the carnitas in the burrito mojado'

dish: carnitas taco / handmade tortillas on fresh nixtamal masa
w: Tortilla factory, grocery and taqueria on Calle 24 since 1953 — daily nixtamal masa and hand-pressed tortillas; get the carnitas and the huaraches/pupusas.
sources: missionlocal.org/2023/12/keeping-culture-alive-sf-masa-line-lapalma-and-tamales/ — 'In line at La Palma' masa/tamales feature

dish: Sicilian-style cioppino; oysters on the half shell
w: Old-school marble-counter seafood in the Castro since 1977 — famous for a Sicilian-inspired cioppino with garlic bread and Boston clam chowder.
The naturally-leavened country loaf that helped define modern SF sourdough, plus the famous morning bun. Owners won the James Beard pastry award.
sources: James Beard Foundation — Outstanding Pastry Chef award (Elisabeth Prueitt & Chad Robertson), 2008
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tartine — James Beard-winning bakery, 600 Guerrero St

dish: cracked Dungeness crab; oysters; cioppino at the counter
w: An 18-stool marble counter running since 1912 — cracked Dungeness crab, fresh oysters, and the crab/shrimp Louie. No reservations, line out the door.
sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swan_Oyster_Depot — SF institution est. 1912, 1517 Polk St

w: North Beach seafood house whose cauldron of crab, clams, mussels and shrimp over pasta is many locals' pick for the city's best cioppino.

address: 1965 Al Scoma Way, San Francisco, CA 94133
w: Pier-to-plate Fisherman's Wharf institution since 1965; the roasted whole Dungeness crab is the reason to wear a bib.

dish: original San Francisco sourdough; clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl
w: The original SF sourdough — same mother starter since 1849, the city's oldest continuously operating business. Get the clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl.
sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boudin_Bakery — original SF sourdough, 1849 mother starter
boudinbakery.com/boudin-at-the-wharf/ — flagship Fisherman's Wharf bakery, 160 Jefferson St

w: The bar that introduced Irish coffee to the United States in 1952 — still lines up dozens of glasses on the marble at once, near the Hyde St cable car turnaround.
sources: thebuenavista.com — 2765 Hyde St; Irish coffee since 1952

w: A tiny Chinatown alley factory hand-folding thousands of fortune cookies a day since 1962 — watch them off the press and buy them warm.
sources: atlasobscura — Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory, 56 Ross Alley, hand-folded since 1962

w: The all-garlic North Beach novelty institution ('we season our garlic with food') — 40-clove garlic chicken and, yes, garlic ice cream. Touristy but iconic.
California's oldest restaurant (est. 1849) — a wood-paneled Financial District classic for cioppino and mesquite-grilled seafood.
sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tadich_Grill — oldest continuously running restaurant in California, est. 1849

dish: raw oysters on the half shell (Hog Island Sweetwaters)
w: The Ferry Building raw bar from the Tomales Bay oyster farm — some of the sweetest, freshest West Coast bivalves, shucked to order.

dish: roasted whole Dungeness crab; garlic noodles
w: The Sunset District Vietnamese house (An family, since 1971) that invented SF garlic noodles — order them with the pepper-crusted roasted whole crab.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-francisco/reviews/thanh-long — 'invented garlic noodles, still the best in SF'

w: Divisadero cafe milling its own whole-grain flour with Josey Baker Bread — the destination for SF's cult thick-cut sourdough toast. TEMPORARILY CLOSED after a June 29, 2026 fire; verify before visiting.

dish: It's-It ice cream sandwich (vanilla between oatmeal cookies, dark-chocolate dipped)
w: The SF-born ice cream sandwich (invented 1928 at Playland-at-the-Beach) — buy them fresh at the Burlingame factory shop where they're made.
sources: kqed.org/food/1337457 — the story of the It's-It ice cream sandwich
